result.topic_en: Latin notes deriving, from conditions on the coefficients a_{μι} (the Riemann-tensor-like condition for the heat-conduction prize problem), that ∂ω_μ/∂x_ν − ∂ω_ν/∂x_μ is homogeneous of order −1 and hence vanishes, leading to symmetry conditions and vanishing of coefficients and their derivatives at the origin.
result.transcription:
[-unde sequitur
$\Theta^{\nu}_{\mu} = -\Theta^{\mu}_{\nu} = \frac{\partial\omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu} - \frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu}$
esse functionem homogeneam ordinis $-1$; porro
$\sum_\nu \Theta^{\nu}_{\mu} x_\nu = \ldots \partial\omega_\mu \quad \omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \Theta^{\iota}_{\mu} x_\iota = \partial\omega_\mu, \ldots \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial x_\mu}$
et quia $\sum_{\mu,\iota} \Theta^{\iota}_{\mu} x_\iota x_\mu = 0$
$2\omega = \sum_\mu x_\mu \partial\omega_\mu = D\omega$
unde concludimus, $\omega$ esse functionem homogeneam ordinis [?]-]
[-At si supponamus, coefficientes-]
[-At si supponitur, coëfficientes $a_{\mu\iota}$ eorumque derivationes in puncto 0 habere valores determinatos finitos, sequitur ebenso $\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu}$, $\omega_\mu$, $\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu}$ in puncto 0 evanescere $\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu}$ habere valorem finitum-]
Hae aequationes alia quadam forma exhiberi possunt, si ponitur brevitatis causa:
$\omega_\mu = \sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} x_\iota \quad ; \quad \frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = a_{\mu\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota$
unde aequatio 2* formam induit.
$\omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial\omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota = 2\sum_\iota \frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota$
Jam si ponitur $2\omega = \sum_\iota \omega_\iota x_\iota \quad 2\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial\omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$, ex hac aequatione sequitur:
$\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota \qquad \frac{\partial^2\omega}{\partial x_\mu \partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial^2\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_\nu} x_\iota$
unde:
$\left(\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial\omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}\right) + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial\left(\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial\omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}\right)}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota = 0$
Quae formula docet $\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial\omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$ esse functionem homogeneam ordinis $-1$. quam per $f(x_1 \ldots x_n)$ designamus. [-est itaque-] habemus itaque
$f(t x_1, t x_2, \ldots t x_n) = t^{-1} f(x_1, x_2 \ldots x_n)$
unde sequitur, posito $t=0$, si quidem supponimus, coefficientes $a_{\iota\iota'}$ [-in puncto-] eorumque derivationes in puncto 0 habere valores determinatos finitos, $f(x_1 x_2 \ldots x_n)$ esse $=0$, vel:
{+ist hier fehlerhaft [?]+}
$\frac{\partial\omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial\omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$
unde porro:
$\sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\nu\iota}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$
Quae simul cum aequationibus [-2-] 2, 2* praebent: \quad unde: $\sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} x_\iota = \sum a_{\mu\iota} x_\iota^0$ [?]
$\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} - \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
Nunc si supponimus esse $a_{\iota\iota'} = a_{\iota'\iota}$ et harum coefficientium {+eorumque derivationum+} valores in puncto $x_\iota = 0$ determinatos et finitos ex aequatione
$\sum a_{\iota\iota'} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
sequitur ter differentiando et posito $x_\iota = 0$:
$a_{\iota\iota'} = 0 \qquad \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_\iota} + \frac{\partial a_{\iota''\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} = 0$
Hinc posito $a_{\iota\iota'} = p_{\mu\iota\iota'}$:
3. $\quad p_{\iota\iota'\iota''} = 0 \qquad \frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial p_{\iota\iota'\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} = 0$ ; in puncto 0.
Quarum prima sequitur, addendo $p_{\iota\iota'\iota''} = 0$:
4. $\quad \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} = 0 \quad$ in puncto 0.
